slides.heading: Looping Through Lists
slides.body: Looping Through Lists is part of Lists and Mutable Sequences. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Looping Through Lists
slides.body: A loop can visit each item in a list. This is useful when you want to print, check, or process every value.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Looping through a list is like reading every name on an attendance sheet.

annotations.note: This line starts a loop that processes each value in a sequence.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Lists use square brackets, zero-based indexes, and can be changed after creation.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Loop through a list of two fruits and print each fruit.
slides.hint: Use for fruit in fruits: then print(fruit).

coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
